headline: Chicago loves the Bulls as a religion of 1991-98 memory, and in 2026 it is a patient, sardonic congregation watching a new size-first rebuild under Splitter.
summary: The Bulls fan base is global because of Jordan but intensely local at its core: South and West Side families who grew up on the dynasty, North Side and suburban season-ticket holders, and a Gen Z that knows the team through The Last Dance and Jordan Brand. Loyalty is to the red-and-black and the idea of 6 banners more than to any roster, so mood tracks front-office credibility rather than wins. Heading into 2026-27, after a 31-51 season, a new regime (coach Tiago Splitter, EVP Bryson Graham) and a young core of Josh Giddey, Matas Buzelis and rookie Caleb Wilson, the feeling is guarded hope mixed with long-running frustration at ownership. Gameday style is jersey-and-throwback culture, with the 1990s as the permanent default.

insights.title: Legacy is the brand, the roster is the guest
insights.detail: Fans wear Jordan 23, Pippen 33 and Rodman 91 to games in numbers that rival current-player jerseys, and the Jordan statue outside the United Center is the pre-game photo spot. Loyalty survives losing seasons because it attaches to the six banners, not the lineup.
insights.implication: Heritage product (1990s cuts, pinstripe-free red/black, Jumpman crossover) will always outsell a pure current-player push; use legacy as the foundation and layer new faces like Buzelis and Wilson on top.

insights.title: A rebuild fan base that has learned to be skeptical
insights.detail: After 31-51 and years of play-in-or-bust middling, supporters are wary of promises and respond to proof: size, development and a visible plan. The new SLAP identity (size, length, athleticism, physicality) gives them a language to rally around.
insights.implication: Frame product around the physicality and 'build' narrative (work-wear textures, heavy fabrics, tough graphic language) rather than hype slogans that the fan base will mock.

insights.title: Two Chicagos in one arena
insights.detail: The upper bowl and neighborhoods carry the Black Chicago heritage of the dynasty and the Public League hoops culture, while lower-bowl corporate and suburban fans buy in bulk. Both identify with the same red-and-black.
insights.implication: Offer a clear price ladder: premium jersey and heritage drops for the lower bowl, accessible tees, hoodies and caps tied to neighborhood and Public League imagery for everyone else, with real local partners.

insights.title: Jordan Brand is family, not a competitor
insights.detail: Chicago treats Jordan and the Jumpman as the home team's own brand; Air Jordan 1 'Chicago' colorways are cultural currency independent of the Bulls. Fans separate buying Jordan from buying team merch.
insights.implication: Coordinate Nike and Jordan Brand launches around the Bulls calendar and avoid cannibalization; a Bulls product that visibly respects the Jordan lineage will be read as authentic.

insights.title: Gen Z knows the era through screens
insights.detail: The Last Dance, retro-jersey fashion and sneaker culture feed a young digital fan base that wears vintage Bulls as streetwear and follows Buzelis and Wilson on social media. Local Public League and high-school hoops also pull teens toward the team.
insights.implication: Launch youth and streetwear capsules through creators, sneaker boutiques and school-hoops moments, not only team channels.

insights.title: The Madhouse ritual is a design asset
insights.detail: The darkened arena, spinning-light starting lineup introduction and the Sirius theme remain the signature gameday moment. Benny the Bull and the red-and-black color blocking are instantly recognized.
insights.implication: Use the lineup-intro lighting, bull-horn and spotlight motifs in graphics and packaging so product feels like it was made in the building.

places.name: Michael Jordan statue
places.why: The bronze Jordan statue is the single most photographed Bulls spot and a pilgrimage for global fans.

places.name: Harold's Chicken Shack

places.name: Navy Pier and the Loop jersey crowd

vocabulary.meaning: Nickname born at Chicago Stadium across Madison Street and carried over to the United Center.
Affectionate, jokey local phrasing, borrowed from Chicago sports comedy.
The instrumental used for lineup introductions, shorthand for the whole ritual.
The 1997-98 season and the 2020 documentary that re-introduced the era to a new generation.
Shorthand for the six championships, used as a standard that current teams are measured against.

designCues.source: The team's primary red and the visual identity of the dynasty
designCues.use: Lead color on jerseys, hoodies and caps; keep it saturated, not orange-shifted.
Use black as the tonal base and white for trim to match the heritage look.

designCues.source: The Bulls primary mark, created in the 1960s
designCues.use: Use official marks only through licensed team product; abstract horn-angle cuts can inform seaming.

designCues.source: Sirius spotlight introduction at the United Center
designCues.use: Spotlight-beam graphics, dark-to-light gradients and glow-in-the-dark details on tees and packaging.

designCues.source: Chicago's steel, rail and stockyard working heritage and the rebuild's physicality message
designCues.use: Heavyweight fleece, canvas, ripstop panels and reinforced stitching for outerwear.
Chunky block numbers and arched name lettering on throwbacks and warm-ups.

designCues.source: Jordan Brand identity tied to Chicago
designCues.use: Co-branded Jordan/Bulls details on select pieces only, coordinated with Jordan Brand.

productHooks: A dynasty-era heritage collection: throwback warm-up jackets, shooting shirts and snapbacks using the 1990s red/black proportions.
A 'Madhouse' lineup-intro capsule with spotlight graphics and glow details, timed to the home opener.
Rookie and young-core player tees and jerseys for Wilson, Buzelis and Giddey, plus a youth line.
A Public League hoops capsule built with Chicago partners (Simeon and local high-school programs, with permission) tying heavy-duty textures to neighborhood hoops.
Jordan Brand x Bulls gameday pieces coordinated for the global-visitor corridor downtown.
watchouts: Jordan Brand and the Jordan estate/likeness and any Jordan-era player imagery require licensing; do not use player names or likenesses without it.
Avoid caricature or crime-stereotype shorthand for the South and West Sides; credit and pay local partners and schools for neighborhood imagery.
Fans are skeptical of ownership and hype; avoid messaging that overpromises a title window.
Do not rebrand around a rebuild slogan that could be mocked if results lag.

segments.name: Dynasty-era diehards
segments.description: Longtime Chicagoans who lived the 1991-98 titles, many from South and West Side families with multi-generation season tickets.
segments.wears: Authentic Jordan, Pippen and Rodman jerseys, vintage snapbacks, red jackets.
segments.reach: Local radio and TV, bars, community events, legacy drops.

segments.name: Families and suburban fans
segments.description: Households from the suburbs who attend a few games a year, driven by kids and the mascot.
segments.wears: Current red icon jerseys, tees, hoodies, youth gear.
segments.reach: Team store, Dick's/Fanatics retail, school and holiday campaigns.

segments.name: Gen Z digital fans
segments.description: Younger fans who grew up on The Last Dance, sneaker culture and social feeds.
segments.wears: Vintage and retro Bulls as streetwear, Jordan footwear, player tees for Buzelis and Wilson.
segments.reach: Instagram, TikTok, Reddit, creators, sneaker boutiques.

segments.name: Global and tourist fans
segments.description: International fans, especially from Asia and Europe, who come to Chicago for the Jordan legacy.
segments.wears: Jordan-era jerseys, Bulls caps, souvenir tees.
segments.reach: Downtown retail, Chicago Sports Museum, travel hubs, online.

segments.name: Corporate and premium
segments.description: Loop and suburban professionals with club seats and sponsor ties.
segments.wears: Premium quarter-zips, subtle red-and-black, authentic jerseys.

extra.sentiment: Guarded hope: fans are tired of mediocrity after a 31-51 season, but the new regime, the size-first plan and the rookie Caleb Wilson give them something to watch. Ownership frustration persists, and expectations are low in national rankings.
extra.gamedayLook: Red or black Bulls jerseys (Jordan 23, Pippen 33, and current Giddey/Buzelis), vintage 1990s tees and snapbacks, Jordan sneakers, and a red or black hoodie in cold months.
